narrator.instruct: Fast-paced, energetic, punchy explainer narrator. Brisk delivery with no long pauses.

manager.instruct: Calm, sly airport manager sharing a trade secret, quick and pleased with herself.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You land in Houston and start walking. The hallway just keeps going.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: By the time you reach baggage claim, your suitcase is already rolling out.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Perfect timing. You feel so lucky.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then a staff door swings open. A manager is dragging your gate to the far end of the map.

lines.speaker: manager
lines.text: Keep them walking. They never complain.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: This airport used to drown in complaints about waiting for bags.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So they hired more baggage handlers, and the wait fell to eight minutes.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then someone timed it. One minute of walking, seven minutes standing at the belt.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The problem wasn't the wait. It was the standing.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So they moved the arrival gates away and sent the bags to the farthest belt.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Now passengers walked six times longer, and complaints dropped to almost zero.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In nineteen eighty-five, a waiting expert wrote the rule down. Busy time feels shorter than empty time.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It's why one hotel put mirrors next to its slow elevators.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Guests fixed their hair, and the complaints stopped.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Your wait never got shorter. It just got hidden in your legs.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Next trip, your gate is the farthest again. You smile the whole way.
